message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it was right or wrong for me to delete my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch. Let me start by going through the situation step by step. First, at the beginning of the school year, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip. I brought my Switch because my school is more than an hour away, and I wanted something to do during the train commute. My stepbrother really wanted to play on it, and since he was into it, it helped distract him while I studied. So, I made a new profile for him so he wouldn't mess up my saves. That seemed like a good idea at the time because it kept things organized and prevented any accidental deletions or changes to my games. When I got back to school, I started getting annoyed because every time I wanted to play a game or go to the eShop, I had to click on my profile. It was a minor inconvenience, but it annoyed me enough that I just deleted his profile. I didn't think much about it because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit, so I didn't expect him to use it again. Then, during Thanksgiving, I brought my Switch again for the train ride. My stepbrother picked it up to play, came into the kitchen where I was talking with my dad, and started freaking out because his Zelda save was gone. He wanted me to help him fix it, and when I told him I deleted it, he started crying, though not full-on crying, just his eyes were watery and red. Now he's holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knew my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn't think it was a big deal because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit. So, was it right or wrong to delete his profile? Let me think about the different aspects. First, ownership: The Switch is mine, so technically, I have the right to delete any profiles on it. But just because I can, does that mean I should? It's a shared device in the sense that my stepbrother used it when I was watching him. But I made a profile for him, which shows that I was considering his needs at the time. When I got back to school, I found it annoying to switch profiles. That's a valid point, but maybe there's a better way to handle it. For example, I could have just logged out of his profile or set a default profile. Deleting it was a more permanent solution, which might have been too harsh. Emotional impact: My stepbrother was upset when he found out his save was gone. He was crying, which shows that it affected him emotionally. Even though I didn't think it was a big deal, it clearly was for him. My dad also thinks it was mean, which adds another perspective. Consideration: I should have considered how my actions would affect others, especially since my stepbrother was using the Switch. Deleting his profile without discussing it first was probably insensitive. It's important to communicate and find a solution that works for both parties. Long-term relationship: My actions might have strained my relationship with my stepbrother and my dad. It's important to maintain good relationships, especially with family. Being more considerate and understanding can help prevent such issues in the future. Alternative solutions: Instead of deleting the profile, I could have talked to my stepbrother about the inconvenience and found a compromise. Maybe he could use the Switch less frequently, or I could set up a way to quickly switch profiles without it being a hassle. That way, both of our needs are met. In conclusion, while I had the right to manage my Switch, deleting the profile without considering my stepbrother's feelings and the impact it would have was wrong. It's important to communicate and find a solution that respects everyone's feelings and needs.
